13:00 Local Time, 07:30 GMT, 13:00 IST: The series has already produced more than enough batting fireworks and the third ODI arrives with India 2-0 up. Virat Kohli’s 139 in the first game, Rohit Sharma’s 101 in the second and Shubman Gill’s unbeaten 223 in Guwahati have proven just how dominant India’s batting has been. Gill’s double-century, completed in only 117 balls, was the centrepiece of a record chase as India hunted down 406 with eight wickets and 39 balls to spare.

West Indies, though, have hardly been short of runs. Their 405 for 7 in Guwahati was their highest total in men’s ODIs, with John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo all scoring hundreds in the same innings. It was a remarkable batting effort from West Indies, with three of their batters reaching centuries, but even a total of 405 for 7 could not prevent India from completing another emphatic run chase.

Now the series moves to New Chandigarh, where the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium will host its first men’s ODI. With the result of the series already decided, India have the luxury of looking at the bigger picture, while West Indies have one last chance to put together the kind of all-round performance that has so far eluded them. After two games dominated by the bat, the question is whether the final ODI can offer something different.
